brief.summary: Three successive advisories put Cyclone Remal ashore on the northern Bay of Bengal coast near the India–Bangladesh border around 20:00 UTC on 26 May, and news reports of West Bengal landfall warnings and Kolkata flight suspensions tell the same story. The track has held steady, but this replay has no river forecasts and uses final rather than as-issued GDACS intensity values.

reasons.text: All three advisories steer the storm north toward roughly 21.5–22.3N, 88.9–89.5E, and the computed landfall is about 20 hours out at 21.8N 89.03E in the northern Bay of Bengal.

The track moved only 13.4 km and the arrival time only 0.3 hours between the last two advisories, though the largest shift across advisories was 54.7 km, so the exact landfall point could still move along the border coast.
GDACS rates the event Orange with 102 km/h winds, enough to be damaging, but these are final reprocessed values and may differ from what was shown at the time.
Independent news reports describe landfall in West Bengal on 26 May, preparedness warnings, NDRF deployment and suspended flights in Kolkata, matching the advisory timing and location.
